gaps.sentence: At midnight, the protesters ___ outside the parliament, refusing to move.
gaps.hint: at midnight, in progress at that point
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific past moment takes the past continuous: were standing.

gaps.sentence: They ___ so much since they started the new school.
gaps.hint: since they started with present result
gaps.explanation: Change measured from a past starting point to now takes the present perfect: have grown.

gaps.sentence: Why ___ sunglasses? It is dark in here.
gaps.hint: happening now with a visible reason
gaps.explanation: The speaker asks about something visibly happening now, so the present continuous fits: are you wearing.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our cousins in Melbourne next month — the flights are booked.
gaps.hint: a booked arrangement for next month
gaps.explanation: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: are visiting.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me yesterday to say she had arrived safely.
gaps.hint: yesterday fixes a finished past action
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the past simple is used: phoned.

gaps.sentence: Be quiet! The baby ___ in the next room.
gaps.hint: be quiet means an action in progress
gaps.explanation: The request for quiet shows an action happening at this moment, so use the present continuous: is sleeping.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: I ___ here for two years, so I know the system well.
gaps.hint: for two years continuing until now
gaps.explanation: 'For two years' with present relevance takes the present perfect, often continuous: have been working.
